source.snippet: I am about to start a bigger project with several subprojects and want to be a human in the loop of otherwise fairly automated loop, which should ideally use different agents for different roles (coding, design, testing, supervision, etc). I know this approach is becoming increasingly common and I wonder if there's already some tooling that facilitates that? Or do you simply use some specific model as a coordinator? [5 points, 4 comments, June 26 2026]

problem_statement: Professional developers and technical solopreneurs running multi-agent AI workflows lack lightweight, configurable orchestration tooling that keeps a human checkpointed in the loop across specialized agents (coder, designer, tester, supervisor), forcing them to wire up fragile custom scripts or rely on heavyweight enterprise platforms.
target_segment: Independent developers, technical solopreneurs, and small dev teams building AI-assisted software projects with multi-agent workflows
notes: Poster is starting a real project ('bigger project with several subprojects'), not purely curious — implies professional context. Market signal is fresh (June 26 2026, 5 points, 4 comments). Existing tools (LangGraph, CrewAI, etc.) are either too low-level or too enterprise-heavy. A paid SaaS orchestration layer targeting solo operators and small teams with a clear human-approval UI could charge per seat/project. Willingness to pay not explicit but professional project context and the 'increasingly common' framing suggest active demand.
